symptom: TestApp round trip: re-executing `describe consumed rest service Mappings.RestClient` (a Studio Pro-authored service, nothing changed) rewrote the unit: `/Operations[0]: 3 -> 2`, `/Operations[1](Request)/Headers[0]: 3 -> 2`, `/Operations[1](Request)/Parameters[0]: 3 -> 2` — law getput, surfaced the moment `Response: json` started to parse
cause: consumed_rest_write.go registered marker 2 for Rest$RestOperation, Rest$HeaderWithValueTemplate and Rest$OperationParameter lists (and the mandatory empty Operations/Headers/Parameters lists), copied from the legacy serializer in the parity port and never measured; Studio Pro writes 3 for those three and 2 only for QueryParameters
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/consumed_rest_write.go` (init registrations), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/consumed_rest_edit.go` (the ALTER splice keeps the stored Operations marker); test `mdl/backend/modelsdk/consumed_rest_markers_test.go`; `mdl/roundtrip/testapp_allowlist_test.go` (Mappings.RestClient struck)
insight: An allowlisted failure at one law can hide a failure at the next: Mappings.RestClient sat on the allowlist as 'breaks parse' since it joined the harness, so nobody ever executed its describe output, and the wrong markers had nothing to fail against. Fixing the parse is what exposed them — expect the outcome of a struck allowlist entry to move one law down, not to go green. Two independent Studio Pro measurements settle a marker cheaply when the census projects are not at hand: the stored bytes of a Studio Pro-authored fixture (TestApp, 11.14.0) and `mx convert -p` of an mxcli-written project (11.6.6), which re-serializes exactly the non-canonical units; they agreed field for field (3/3/3, QueryParameters 2, Tags 1). A comment saying a value 'mirrors the legacy serializer' is a flag that it was never measured
